title: Local factorization of units on an integral generic fibre
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a flat local homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] of commutative Noetherian integral domains [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with $A$ normal [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Here local means that $A,B$ each have a unique maximal ideal and the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $B$ is the maximal ideal of $A$. Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and identify $A,B,K$ with their images in $\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ under this injective map. Assume that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$, the ring obtained from $B/\mathfrak pB$ by inverting all images of $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ is a nonzero integral domain; these are the integral nonempty fibres. Put $B_K=(A\setminus\{0\})^{-1}B$, the ring of fractions $b/a$ with $b\in B$ and $0\ne a\in A$. Then every $f\in B_K^\times$ can be written $f=h u$ with $h\in K^\times$ and $u\in B^\times$. The factor $h$ is unique modulo $A^\times$: if $f=h u=h'u'$ with $u,u'\in B^\times$, then $h/h'\in A^\times$. In particular, for $h\in K^\times$, its image is a unit of $B$ if and only if $h\in A^\times$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, proof, affine/local ring factorization paragraph: from s=a/r=r_prime/a_prime through the symbolic-power ideals I,I_prime and s=u g/r. The unit-reflection uniqueness is the same proof's uniqueness for a faithfully flat local map. This statement is the local commutative-algebra input, not the conclusion about an invertible sheaf or a Cartier divisor.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak m_A,\mathfrak m_B$ be the maximal ideals. Locality gives $\mathfrak m_AB\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$, so $B/\mathfrak m_AB\ne0$. The local case of the faithful-flatness criterion makes $A\to B$ faithfully flat. Ideal contraction gives $JB\cap A=J$ for every ideal $J\subseteq A$, in particular injectivity. These facts justify all the inclusions into $\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ used below.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, affine paragraph, faithful-flat descent; algebra.tex Tags 00HP (lemma-ff), 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective)

proof.text: For any prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and any $s\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$, multiplication by $s$ on $A/\mathfrak p$ is injective. Flat tensor exactness, identifying $(A/\mathfrak p)\otimes_A B$ with $B/\mathfrak pB$ via $\bar a\otimes b\mapsto\overline{ab}$, makes multiplication by $s$ injective on $B/\mathfrak pB$. Thus $B/\mathfrak pB$ injects into its localization at $A\setminus\mathfrak p$: a class killed by localization is killed by one such $s$ and hence is zero. By the integral nonempty fibre hypothesis this localization is a nonzero domain. Therefore $B/\mathfrak pB$ is a nonzero domain and $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak pB$ is prime. Its contraction is $\mathfrak p$ by step 1. This supplies the justification for the source\'s assertion that $\mathfrak pB$ is prime.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, affine paragraph: q_i=p_iA is prime; algebra.tex Tag 00HD (lemma-flat)

proof.text:
Choose presentations $f=a/r$ and $f^{-1}=a\prime/r\prime$ with $a,a\prime\in B$ and $r,r\prime\in A\setminus\{0\}$. Equality in the fraction field gives $aa\prime=rr\prime=t
e0$. In particular $a,a\prime
e0$. Let $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_n$ be all primes minimal over $(t)$; the set is finite. The principal ideal height bound and $t
e0$ show that each has height one. Their localizations $A_i=A_{\mathfrak p_i}$ are discrete valuation rings by the cited normal-domain valuation statement. Write $m_i=v_{\mathfrak p_i}(t)\geq1$. If $t$ is a unit the list is empty; every ideal intersection below then means the whole ring.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, affine paragraph s=a/r and s=r_prime/a_prime; algebra.tex Tags 00FR, 00KV, 031S, 00PD

proof.text: For each $i$ choose a uniformizer $\pi_i\in A_i$. Set $\mathfrak q_i=\mathfrak p_iB$. Since $\mathfrak q_i\cap A=\mathfrak p_i$, the fraction rule defines $A_i\to B_i=B_{\mathfrak q_i}$. The maximal ideal of $B_i$ is $\mathfrak q_iB_i=\mathfrak p_iB_i=\pi_iB_i$. The ring $B_i$ is a Noetherian local domain: use localization permanence for Noetherianity, and the fraction construction for the domain assertion. The image of $\pi_i$ is nonzero and is a nonunit. The unit-times-power lemma therefore gives $a=u_i\pi_i^{e_i}$ and $a\prime=u_i\prime\pi_i^{e_i\prime}$ in $B_i$ with units $u_i,u_i\prime$ and nonnegative integers $e_i,e_i\prime$. In $A_i$ the same lemma writes $t=w_i\pi_i^{m_i}$ with a unit $w_i$ (the exponent equals the normalized valuation from step 3). Its image is still a unit in $B_i$. Cancelling powers in $aa\prime=t$ proves $e_i+e_i\prime=m_i$: unequal exponents would make a positive power of the nonunit $\pi_i$ a unit.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, affine paragraph: the two local DVRs, ramification index 1, and e_i+e_i_prime; algebra.tex Tags 00FN, 00PD

proof.text: For a prime $P$ of a ring $T$ write $P^{(j)}=\{x\in T:x/1\in P^jT_P\}$ for $j\geq0$. We claim $\bigcap_i\mathfrak p_i^{(m_i)}=(t)$. One inclusion follows from $tA_i=\mathfrak p_i^{m_i}A_i$. Conversely take $x$ in the intersection and consider its class in $A/tA$. Every associated prime of $A/tA$ has height one by the cited normal-domain quotient theorem. It contains $t$ (it is the annihilator of a class modulo $t$), and hence is minimal over $(t)$: a smaller prime containing $t\ne0$ would give a chain of length two starting at $(0)$. It is therefore one of the $\mathfrak p_i$. The class of $x$ vanishes in all these localizations, because $x\in tA_i$. The cited injectivity into the product of associated-prime localizations gives $x\in(t)$. This also proves the claim for the empty list, when $A/tA=0$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, displayed intersection for (rr_prime); algebra.tex Tags 031T (lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1), 0311 (lemma-zero-at-ass-zero)

proof.text: Set $I=\bigcap_i\mathfrak p_i^{(e_i)}$ and $I\prime=\bigcap_i\mathfrak p_i^{(e_i\prime)}$. For $x\in I$ and $y\in I\prime$, localization at $\mathfrak p_i$ puts $xy$ in $\mathfrak p_i^{e_i+e_i\prime}A_i=\mathfrak p_i^{m_i}A_i$. Step 5 gives $xy\in(t)$. Finite sums of such products give $II\prime\subseteq(t)$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, affine paragraph defining I,I_prime and observing II_prime contained in (rr_prime)

proof.text: Extension to $B$ preserves these finite intersections. Indeed for any finite family of ideals $J_i\subseteq A$, the sequence $0\to\bigcap_iJ_i\to A\to\bigoplus_i A/J_i$, with the quotient maps as components, is exact. Flat tensor exactness identifies its tensor with $0\to(\bigcap_iJ_i)\otimes_A B\to B\to\bigoplus_iB/J_iB$. The image of the left map is $(\bigcap_iJ_i)B$, whereas the kernel of the right map is $\bigcap_iJ_iB$; the quotient identification sends $\bar x\otimes b$ to $\overline{xb}$. For an empty family both sides are $B$. Now apply symbolic-power flat extension to each prime pair $(\mathfrak p_i,\mathfrak q_i)$ from step 2. This yields $IB=\bigcap_i\mathfrak q_i^{(e_i)}$ and $I\prime B=\bigcap_i\mathfrak q_i^{(e_i\prime)}$. The local factorizations of step 4 place $a$ in $IB$ and $a\prime$ in $I\prime B$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, equalities for IA and I_prime A; algebra.tex Tags 0BBY (lemma-flat-intersect-ideals), 0BC0 (lemma-symbolic-power-flat-extension)

proof.text: Step 6 gives $(II\prime)B\subseteq tB$, while $t=aa\prime\in(IB)(I\prime B)=(II\prime)B$ gives the reverse inclusion. Here extension commutes with ideal multiplication directly by expanding finite sums of generators. Contracting both ideals by faithful flatness gives $II\prime=(t)$ in $A$. We now use locality to write out the principal-product argument. Express $t=\sum_{j=1}^N x_jy_j$ with $x_j\in I$, $y_j\in I\prime$. Since every $x_jy_j\in(t)$, write $x_jy_j=c_jt$; cancellation of $t\ne0$ gives $\sum c_j=1$. Some $c_j$ is a unit, as otherwise the sum belongs to the maximal ideal. Set $g=x_j$, $g\prime=c_j^{-1}y_j$, so $gg\prime=t$. For any $x\in I$, write $xg\prime=dt=dgg\prime$ with $d\in A$ and cancel $g\prime\ne0$ to obtain $x=dg$. Thus $I=(g)$. Interchanging the factors gives $I\prime=(g\prime)$. This is the elementary local proof of the special case of Tag 09ME used here; no invertible-module theorem is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, descent of the product ideal; algebra.tex Tag 09ME (lemma-product-ideals-principal), local proof with one unit coefficient

proof.text: Since $a\in IB=gB$ and $a\prime\in I\prime B=g\prime B$, choose $u,u\prime\in B$ with $a=gu$ and $a\prime=g\prime u\prime$. Then $t=aa\prime=gg\prime uu\prime=tuu\prime$ and cancellation in $B$ gives $uu\prime=1$. Thus $u\in B^\times$. With $h=g/r\in K^\times$ we obtain $f=hu$, as required.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, end of affine paragraph: a=ug, a_prime=u_prime g_prime, s=ug/r

proof.text: For unit reflection on fractions let $h=c/d\in K^\times$ with $c,d\in A\setminus\{0\}$ and assume $h\in B^\times$. Then $c=dh$ implies $c\in dB\cap A=dA$, hence $h\in A$. Likewise $d=ch^{-1}$ implies $d\in cB\cap A=cA$, hence $h^{-1}\in A$. Thus $h\in A^\times$; the converse follows by mapping an inverse. Finally if $f=hu=h\prime u\prime$ then $h/h\prime=u\prime/u\in B^\times$ and the reflection just proved gives $h/h\prime\in A^\times$. This proves both remaining clauses without any normality hypothesis beyond the one already used for existence.
